task_description:
Given a real GitHub issue and the project's codebase at the commit where the issue was
filed, an automated technique attempts to generate a test that reproduces the bug
described in the issue.
candidate_definition: ONE instance = ONE merged pull request that closes a reported issue and, in the same PR, adds or modifies at least one test that fails at the commit before the PR merged and passes at the commit that merged it. The instance is identified by {repository URL, merge_commit} where merge_commit is the commit that merged the PR (produced by any of GitHub's three merge styles: merge commit, squash, or rebase) and base_commit is merge_commit's FIRST parent. A single-parent merging commit (squash/rebase) is a normal, valid candidate; a second parent is never required.
source_requirements:
Real, public Python projects with an issue tracker and pull requests. ONE instance = ONE
merged pull request, identified by {repository URL, the commit that merged it}. Candidate =
a merged pull request that closes an issue and, in the same PR, adds or modifies a test: that
test fails when run against the commit before the PR was merged and passes when run against
the commit that merged it.

HOW THE PULL REQUEST WAS MERGED DOES NOT MATTER, and the instance must not require one style
over another. GitHub offers three merge buttons and projects differ: a merge commit has two
parents, the PR's work on the second; a squash merge and a rebase merge land the PR as ONE
ORDINARY COMMIT with a single parent. All three are valid candidates here. In every case the
merging commit is the postfix side and its FIRST PARENT is the base commit, which is the
prefix side -- for a squashed or rebased PR the first parent is simply its only parent. Do
not require the merging commit to have a second parent: that clause alone excludes every
project that squashes, which is a large share of the Python ecosystem. The two commits are recorded
under the names merge_commit (the commit that merged the pull request) and base_commit
(its first parent), whichever of the three merge styles produced them.
criteria: real merged pull request that closes a reported issue, merged in any of the three ways GitHub offers (merge commit, squash, rebase); the merging commit's first parent is the base commit in all three, and a single-parent merging commit is normal, not a defect the PR's own added/modified test fails on the pre-fix commit and passes on the PR's merge commit, confirmed by an actual test run both the pre-fix and post-fix snapshots build/install and run their test suite the builder verifies itself, by running it on its own machine, that the PR's test fails on the prefix version and passes on the postfix version, and that the PR changes non-test source; it records the test's id and its judgment in builder_notes done means: the harness ran every script on a blank machine without a crash, and the builder has verified the points above itself and written what it verified, with the numbers and the reason for anything it accepted against the harness's observations, into instance.json under builder_notes. The harness reports what it observed; the builder judges.
criteria_list: real merged pull request that closes a reported issue, merged in any of the three ways GitHub offers (merge commit, squash, rebase); the merging commit's first parent is the base commit in all three, and a single-parent merging commit is normal, not a defect
the PR's own added/modified test fails on the pre-fix commit and passes on the PR's merge commit, confirmed by an actual test run
both the pre-fix and post-fix snapshots build/install and run their test suite

the builder verifies itself, by running it on its own machine, that the PR's test fails on the prefix version and passes on the postfix version, and that the PR changes non-test source; it records the test's id and its judgment in builder_notes

done means: the harness ran every script on a blank machine without a crash, and the builder has verified the points above itself and written what it verified, with the numbers and the reason for anything it accepted against the harness's observations, into instance.json under builder_notes. The harness reports what it observed; the builder judges.
quality_gates_list: reproducibility: re-verify a sample of instances across 3 clean-environment reruns, requiring identical outcomes

corruption sensitivity: a deliberately corrupted instance/label (e.g. a test_patch whose test passes on prefix) must be rejected by the pipeline's own gates; the declared negative_control (revert_fix.sh on postfix) must flip the postfix verdict
deduplication: near-duplicate instances removed (at most one instance per pull request, and diversity caps applied per repository)
the harness ran every declared script on a blank machine without a crash
instance_format: a directory of scripts under /bench: Dockerfile, setup.sh, instance.json, checkout.sh, apply_patch.sh, install.sh, run_tests.sh, revert_fix.sh; instance.json carries repo_url, merge_commit, base_commit, test_name, problem_statement, builder_notes

examples.description: A merged PR in a public Python project, squash-merged as one ordinary single-parent commit, that closes issue #NNNN and adds test_foo_regression to tests/test_foo.py. base_commit is the squash commit's only parent. The test fails on base_commit+test_patch and passes on the squash commit.
A merged PR landed as a two-parent merge commit; base_commit is the merge commit's FIRST parent (the base branch tip), not the second.
A merged PR that only edits tests with no non-test source change — the fix.patch would be empty, so the fail->pass transition would not be attributable to a source fix.
A PR in django/django — on the excluded SWE-bench/SWT-Bench roster.
